title: Earth Just Got a Health Check — and 7 of 9 Life-Support Systems Are in Trouble
summary:
Imagine going to the doctor and getting a blood test. If the results were really bad, the doctor would send you straight to the hospital. That's basically what a new report says about Earth.

The report is called "Planetary Health Check 2026." More than 60 scientists worked on it. They studied nine "planetary boundaries" — the natural systems that keep Earth stable, like climate, oceans, and forests. When a boundary is crossed, the risk of serious, permanent harm goes up.

Seven of the nine have already been breached. That includes climate change, ocean acidification (when oceans get too acidic), and damage to living things. Two boundaries — the ozone layer and tiny particles in the air — are still in the safe zone globally.

"If you had a patient with a blood test that looks like this, you would send them to the ICU right away," said Niklas Kitzmann, lead editor of the report.

The report also warns about the Amazon rainforest nearing a dangerous tipping point, and damage to the seafloor from fishing and possible deep-sea mining.

But it's not all bad news. Kitzmann says we still have a window to turn things around — especially with cheaper solar power and new treaties protecting oceans and land. "It's not enough yet," he said. "But we shouldn't think that this is a completely unsolvable problem."
why_it_matters: The oceans, forests and climate in this report are the same systems that give us clean air, water and food, so the choices people make now shape the world kids will grow up in.

background_read: Niklas Kitzmann is the lead editor of the report — the person in charge of putting all the scientists' work together.
The ICU (intensive care unit) is the part of a hospital where the most dangerously sick patients go for special, round-the-clock care.
The ozone layer has been a success story: countries around the world agreed in the 1980s to stop making certain chemicals, and the ozone shield is slowly healing.
Article_Structure: WHO: More than 60 scientists who wrote the 'Planetary Health Check 2026' report, with Niklas Kitzmann as lead editor
WHAT: They checked nine planetary boundaries and found that seven have already been breached
WHERE: The check covers the whole planet, with special warnings about the Amazon rainforest and damage to the seafloor from fishing and possible deep-sea mining
WHY: Crossing a boundary raises the risk of serious, permanent harm — but Kitzmann says there is still a window to turn things around

perspectives.description: They point to cheaper solar power and new treaties protecting oceans and land as proof that people can still turn things around.
They say seven out of nine broken boundaries is like a patient who needs the ICU straight away, and warn about the Amazon and the seafloor.
They treat the boundaries as warning lights rather than a countdown timer — how bad things get depends on what people do next.
